The ReAct Cycle in AI Agents: How Agents Think, Act and Watch

The video explains the ReAct cycle, which makes an AI agent reason and act in cycles of thinking, acting and observing. It shows the anatomy of the agent (model, context and tools), how the trajectory accumulates and is sent back to the model every cycle and what conditions close the loop.

  • Agentic engineering

The anatomy of an agent

The video is based on Li Bojie's book on AI agents. According to this material, an agent is more than a language model (LLM): the model needs to be connected to the right context and real tools. Without one of these three pieces, the system loses its autonomy 01:03.

The video uses a metaphor of the body 01:47:

  • LLM is the brain: understands the data, reasons and decides 01:47;
  • the context are the eyes: defines what the agent sees and remembers the environment. 01:47;
  • the tools are hands and feet: allow to act in the world, such as searching the internet, sending a message or running a script 01:47.

What is the ReAct cycle

ReAct brings together two words in English: reasoning and acting. The mechanism removes the agent from the passive position of receiving only one prompt and makes him reason about the problem and act in the environment, one step at a time 02:30.

A modern agent does not expect text in a chat: it is event oriented. Receives stimuli, such as messages or audios in an app, queryes memory and triggers external tools such as reading emails or checking an agenda 02:52.

Think, act and observe

The cycle has three times 03:35:

1. Thinking: the model analyzes the problem and chooses the strategy 03:35. 2. Act: uses a tool to execute the plan 03:35. 3. Observe: evaluates the result that the tool returned, and the cycle resumes 03:35.

The loop only stops when the task is finished 03:56.

This cycle allows you to solve open problems, such as building a software from scratch or doing a dense search, in which you cannot know at first how many steps the task will take. The agent tries a route, observes the result and corrects the path 04:17.

In the code, the JSON blocks show the reasoning of the model becoming called a tool. In the video example, the model mounts the command and calls the function that seeks the current weather in Vancouver 04:39.

The path

With each cycle, the agent accumulates a history, called trajectory 05:00.

The total context of the agent adds two parts 05:00:

  • a static prefix, with the rules: AI personality and tool instructions 05:00;
  • the trajectory: what was requested, what the AI responded, the tools used and the results 05:21.

Language models do not hold state between one call and another (they are stateless). Therefore, the framework involving the agent redirects the entire trajectory to the model every cycle 05:43.

If the infrastructure doesn't resend the history, the AI forgets what it was doing. 06:03.

When to stop

Loop depends on output conditions 06:03:

  • the task ends and the final answer is delivered 06:25;
  • AI decides that it already has enough data and no more tools 06:25;
  • the agent reaches the maximum cycle limit 06:25;
  • errors accumulate, and the framework closes operation by force 06:45.

These locks prevent the agent from spinning endlessly and spending resources for nothing 06:45.

The video closes by asking what changes when these cycles come out of the chat windows and run continuously and invisiblely on mobile phones and computers. Understanding this engine would be the first step towards the next era of computing 07:07.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does ReAct mean?

It is the junction of reasoning and acting: the agent reasons and acts in cycles 02:30.

Why does the agent need to resend his history?

Because the language model doesn't keep state between calls. Without the history, he forgets the task 05:43.

About the video

In this explanatory video, we detailed the operation of the ReAct cycle**, the essential architecture that allows AI Agents to go beyond simple chats.

Understand how integration between the **LLM (Brain)**, the **Context (Eyes)** and the **Tools (Hands and Feet)** enables agents to perform complex tasks by means of continuous iteration: **Think

What are you going to learn in this video:
* ** The Basic Formula**: The central architecture where `Agent = LLM + Context + Tools'.
* ** The Loop ReAct in Practice**: As the model generates Reasoning, it calls external tools (Acting) and analyzes the results (Observing).
* ** Trajectory and Context**: How structured message history guides agent decisions to each cycle iteration.
***Harness Engineering**: The support layer and governance around the model that guarantees reliable executions.
